speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation for your acute diarrhea, have you had any fever or blood in your stool, and how many loose bowel movements have you had in the last 24 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). The history of recent levofloxacin use for pneumonia, combined with acute watery diarrhea (9 episodes) and abdominal cramping, is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. I am requesting your stool for C. difficile toxin assay and a CBC to check for leukocytosis.
